title: Detect stealthy noisy tenant and auto reservation rebalancer prototype
creator: Ava Martinez
description: After the capacity event on 2026-03-08 where a low-profile tenant consumed sustained burst tokens and caused reservation starvation, we need a conservative detection pipeline and an automated reservation rebalancer prototype. The goal is to detect 'stealthy' noisy tenants (long, low-amplitude rate increases) that evade current burst heuristics, reduce false positives on legitimate traffic patterns, and evaluate an automated rebalancer that proposes, validates, and applies reservation adjustments within safety bounds. This ticket covers design, prototype implementation, instrumentation, and a short canary run in a dedicated staging cluster.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Ava Martinez: Initial write-up of incident telemetry and hypothesis attached (link). Observed token-rate drift across 3 hours with tail latency degradation for other tenants. Candidate signals: sustained 95th percentile of per-tenant token/sec above historic baseline, KV cache churn rate, and long-lived accelerator occupancy.

2026-03-11 - Liam Chen: Prototype plan: (1) offline detector that computes rolling-zscore over per-tenant token/sec, (2) spectral-smoothing to ignore bursty traffic, (3) generate anomaly score and confidence. If score > 0.9 AND latency impact observed, propose reservation delta. Start with read-only proposals to ops API.

2026-03-12 - Ravi Patel (PM): PM feedback: keep operator approval path for initial rollout; provide clear rollback and escalation docs. Add cost-safety cap to prevent aggressive rebalancing that inflates running costs.
2026-03-12 - Security review note (SRE): Ensure the rebalancer calls are authenticated and logged; do not expose tenant-level proposals to non-ops users. Logged for audit trail.

2026-03-13 - Design review (Maya Singh): UX: operator console should show the anomaly timeline, proposed delta, expected latency improvement, and confidence band. Add a one-click rollback and 'explain' link to the decision heuristics.

2026-03-14 - Liam Chen: Implemented offline detector and dashboard with sample anomalies. Opened PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1427. Added metric: tenant_reservation_proposal{score,delta,confidence} and alert rule draft.

2026-03-14 - Ava Martinez: Ops runbook draft added: https://confluence.redwood.com/display/INFR/Stealthy+Noisy+Tenant+Runbook. Include steps for manual isolation (cgroup+nvidia-smi pin), proposal vetting, and emergency eviction.
2026-03-14 - QA note (Tessa Nguyen): Need synthetic workload tests that mimic slow ramping high-rate clients. Flagging as blocker for canary until test suite expanded.
actions: A1: Finalize detector threshold tuning using last 6 months of tenant telemetry (owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-03-18)
A2: Implement 'proposal-only' rebalancer mode that writes proposed deltas to the ops queue without applying changes (owner: Liam Chen, ETA: 2026-03-20)

A3: Add cost-safety cap: never increase total reserved capacity by more than 8% per rebalancing window; never reduce a tenant below 30% of historical median reservation (owner: Ava Martinez, ETA: 2026-03-18)
A4: Add audit logging and signed operator approvals for any applied reservation change (owner: Security Team, contact: Jordan Blake, ETA: 2026-03-21)
A5: Create synthetic slow-ramp workload generator and add to e2e test harness for staging canary (owner: Tessa Nguyen, ETA: 2026-03-19)
A6: Canary: run proposal-only rebalancer in staging for 72h, review human-verified proposals, then run small-scale apply mode with strict rollback window (owner: Platform Oncall, ETA: 2026-03-24)
A7: Post-canaary review: if false positive rate < 6% and no customer-facing latency regressions, bundle for release dedicated-2026.03 (owner: Release Lead, ETA: 2026-03-28)
acceptance_criteria: Detector produces candidate proposals with measured precision >= 0.94 on historical labelled incidents and recall >= 0.82 for stealthy patterns
Proposal-only mode runs in staging for 72 hours and generates proposals that are actionable and explainable
Synthetic workload tests detect stealthy patterns reliably and are included in CI for the staging channel
Operators can approve/reject proposals via console with audit trail and one-click rollback
Cost-safety caps prevent total reserved capacity growth > 8% during rebalancer operation
resolution_summary: This ticket scopes a cautious, observable approach: detect stealthy noisy tenants with a conservative anomaly scorer, run a proposal-only rebalancer in staging, expand telemetry and synthetic tests, and then canary a low-impact apply mode guarded by cost-safety caps and operator approval. Goal is to reduce eviction-induced tail latency for co-tenants while avoiding unnecessary reservation churn or cost spikes.
